answer: Sybil resistance binds each identity to bonded collateral and observes joint signing patterns: when k coordinated identities equivocate, correlated penalties scale as O(k^2), so duplicating agents raises exposure faster than membership. Detection then applies an exponential capital-loss multiplier to the swarm, while asymmetric depreciation prevents recovery through cheap replacement. An island cannot evade the anchor, and a falcon identity offers no safe disguise.
